statement: No explicit witness bound has been accepted yet. Reference point (recorded, not accepted): assuming H(theta) (no zeros of any Dirichlet L-function with Re s > theta), a Bach-type argument should give deterministic Miller-Rabin in (log n)^(2 + 1/(1-theta) + o(1)) bit operations. With the best published theta = 8748867/10000000 (Xu-Sang, conditional on OpenAI's inputs) the exponent is exactly 12502266/1251133 = 9.99275536...; with theta = 7/8 it is 10. That argument has not been written out with explicit constants (no explicit C exists), so this is not yet an algorithm.

metric.name: mr_exponent (then C, D, n0 for explicit bounds)

scope: Bit complexity on a multitape Turing machine, Harvey-van der Hoeven multiplication. Conditional on H(theta). For comparison: Lenstra-Pomerance AKS is (log n)^(6+o(1)) unconditionally; under GRH (theta = 1/2) this method gives 4.

assumptions.statement: H(7/8): OpenAI, 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re(s) > 7/8' (2026-09-30). Not peer reviewed; the statement (not the proof's applications) is formalized in Lean (lean/ComparatorChallenges/DirichletSevenEighths.lean).
theta = 8748867/10000000 (Xu-Sang, arXiv:2610.15291), assuming the analytic inputs of A1. Not peer reviewed.
The preprint's statement covers every modulus q and every Dirichlet character (including imprimitive ones, via Euler factors), uniformly, as docs/template-T1.md requires.
Lemma T1 (docs/template-T1.md) holds with explicit constants: the Bach-type transfer from H(theta) to a witness bound. This is the project's core task.

Every odd composite n < psi_13 = 3317044064679887385961981 has a strong witness among the first 13 primes (Sorenson-Webster, Math. Comp. 86 (2017) 985-1003). Peer reviewed; sanity-checked by verify/check.py smalln.
